Maya (Product): Follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A: trying to be explicit about how quotas/credits behave during short deploy windows. Questions: do we have an established "deploy burst" flow? What happens if a canary causes token spikes? What are support timelines for temporary quota bumps? /cc @Ravi

Ravi (Finance): TL;DR: usage is billed as consumed; we can perform manual adjustments. For predictable events (scheduled deploys) open a support ticket 48h ahead and we can authorize temporary credits or quota increases for hosted accounts. Dedicated customers have an expedited path via their TAM.

Jude (Eng): Tech nuance: canaries route a small fraction to new model variant. If that variant costs more per token, you'll see higher unit spend even at small traffic %. Quotas don't auto-expand during deploys. Also beware client retries during failovers can multiply requests. Recommend honoring 429s.

Maya (Product): So no automatic short-lived bursts yet. Any plan to change that?

Sam (CEO): We want a safe automated burst feature long-term, but it needs guardrails (hard caps, anomaly detection). For now manual only. Prioritize preventing runaway customer bills.

Olivia (SRE): Ops tip: if you anticipate deploy-induced traffic, create a brief deploy-ops runbook and tag it for quota review. We can prioritize those tickets. Also runbook should include expected qps and duration.

Maya (Product): Can we get an alert when an org is within 10% of quota before a deploy? Would be handy to pause.

Ravi (Finance): We have account-level alerts; Jude can surface route-level cost thresholds in Console today. I'll work to add a "pre-deploy" alert template.

Jude (Eng): Another mitigation: caching prefixes and freeze churn on prompts during canary. If you can freeze variable prompt fields, token delta drops a lot. Also consider ramping canary slower.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: web-api v2.4.1 -> canary 7% at 16:22 UTC

Maya (Product): For migrations that spawn background inference jobs, what's recommended?

Olivia (SRE): Schedule background batches off-peak or run them through our batch endpoints which consume quota differently and can be rate-limited. If unavoidable, request a temporary quota bump and we'll coordinate a safe window.

Jude (Eng): Example console alert pseudo-snippet Maya asked for:
```
# pseudo rule
when(cost_last_10m > expected_baseline * 1.5)
notify(["#deploy-ops","team-owner@example.com"])
```

Maya (Product): Great — can you add that to the docs? Also please include example language for support tickets so PMs know what to include.

Ravi (Finance): Action: I'll draft a short FAQ + example ticket template. Ticket FIN-834 created (deploy-burst-policy).

Sam (CEO): Action items recap: (1) Ravi to propose manual burst policy + ticket template, (2) Eng/Jude to expose pre-deploy alert toggle in Console, (3) Product to publish best-practice checklist. We'll reconvene in two weeks.

Maya (Product): Thanks everyone. Please ping me on the doc so I can weave into the product playbook. :sparkles:

Ravi (Finance): Will do.
